errors.text: The proposed tribo-oxidation mechanism requires an oxygen-containing atmosphere, whereas the target is an atomistic nanoindentation/friction simulation with no oxidation chemistry represented.
The temperature boundary is expressed near 800–900 °C rather than the target threshold of approximately 900 K, a difference of several hundred kelvin.

The predicted trend is opposite to the target: the hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature wear behavior, while the target shows stable performance only through 600 K and sharp deterioration at and above 900 K.

The proposed thermally induced FCC-to-HCP transition is not supported by the cited evidence; E4 instead reports HCP-to-FCC conversion upon heating, while E3 requires extreme pressure to induce FCC-to-HCP transformation.
An increased count of locally HCP-coordinated atoms in the target should not automatically be interpreted as a bulk FCC-to-HCP phase transition.
